title: CB-03's new `environment_retryable` class duplicates `infrastructure_transient` and breaks the closed classification contract in a file no node may touch
detail: The base harness already has exactly the mechanism CB-03 proposes: `classify_verification_failure` (harness_labs/feature_run.py:404-423) emits `infrastructure_transient`, and `_verify_with_recovery` gives that class free re-runs that consume neither a repair dispatch nor the repair budget (feature_run.py:1324 `env_retries = 0`, 1367-1375 `classification == "infrastructure_transient" and env_retries < 2 -> continue`). AC-CB03-1 nevertheless mandates a NEW classification name. That name is not free: `_CLASS_LIMITS` in harness_labs/plan_graph_budget.py:47-54 is a closed set, and `RetryBudgetLedger.import_child_evidence` raises `BudgetError("structured child command has invalid classification")` for any command failure whose classification is outside it (plan_graph_budget.py:296-298; same for repair dispatches at 309). PlanGraph propagates that as a fatal `PlanGraphError` (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:1192-1198), i.e. a whole-graph crash. plan_graph_budget.py is in NO node's allowed_paths (contract-burden-decomposition.json:64-465), so CB-03 as scoped cannot make the new class legal. The necessary change is ~4 lines inside the existing `infrastructure_transient` branch — add `timed_out is True`, `exit_code == 124`, and negative/143 signal exits as additional rule_ids under the class that already exists — with no new vocabulary, no new budget plumbing, and no cross-file breakage.

title: AC-CB03-2 and AC-CB03-3 are already true of the frozen base, so they cannot be demonstrated red
detail: AC-CB03-2 requires 'a bounded, audited environment-retry allowance without dispatching a repair executor and without consuming the repair budget' — that is verbatim the base behavior at feature_run.py:1367-1375, bounded twice over (env_retries < 2, and the loop cap `range(1, repair_limit + 4)` at feature_run.py:1329). AC-CB03-3 requires 'the classification of every failure is recorded in the audit journal' — base already does this at feature_run.py:1348-1356 (`recorded["failure"] = classify_verification_failure(command)` then `audit.append("deterministic_verification_completed", ...)`). Under program rule 1 every criterion must be provable by a test that fails on base; two of CB-03's three substantive criteria are unfalsifiable there. Either they are restatements that should be dropped (leaving CB-03 as a rules-only extension, which is its real content), or the node will be pushed to invent new substrate purely to make a red test possible.

title: CB-05's adoption grant collapses to the `allow_dirty_baseline` flag this program's own launcher already sets — the receipt binding is vacuous as written
detail: AC-CB05-1 admits a dirty baseline when every dirty path is covered by 'the receipted change set OR the task's writable paths'. The second disjunct swallows the first: writable_paths for repair/fix dispatches are exactly `node.run.allowed_paths` (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:436,516,552), and the preflight already refuses out-of-scope writes post-hoc via `paths_outside_scope`. So the new 'audited runtime adoption grant' is behaviorally identical to `allow_dirty_baseline=True`, which is not a hard-frozen escape hatch at all — it is an ordinary constructor field (harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py:66,129-136; harness_labs/controller_live.py:155,221-224) that THIS launcher already sets on every writable executor (run_burden_plan_graph.py:414, 506, 553). The load-bearing part of item 5 is receipt-scoped admission; the plan should delete the writable-paths disjunct or the node builds a grant protocol across three modules for a config default. Additionally there is a third `allow_dirty_baseline` site, harness_labs/agent_mixture.py:107,132-133,248, which is in no node's allowed_paths — the grant would cover two of three executor construction paths.

title: CB-06 builds new kernel adjudication for a dead-end the shipped harness does not create
detail: The pg88 evidence is quoted from the operator's launcher prose ('this build segment is explicitly prohibited from dispatching verification-only tasks or rerunning that command' — contract-burden-reduction.md:72,102-104), not from a harness gate. The standard dispatch schema this program itself uses ships a dedicated `verify` segment immediately after `build` (harness_labs/feature_run_policy.py:185-217), whose coordinator is instructed to 'Run the declared acceptance and regression checks against the actual candidate'. Criteria can therefore be satisfied by task coverage in that segment through the existing path (harness_labs/controller_kernel.py:1027-1036), and `run.complete` requires all criteria satisfied only at the end (controller_kernel.py:917-918). Before adding a new criterion kind, a kernel adjudication path, and a change to the plan-graph bound completion path, CB-06 needs a red test showing the block is forced by harness code under the standard schema. If it is not, the fix is a segment-configuration correction in the offending launcher — a deletion, not a mechanism.

title: CB-07's new `deliverable_floor.py` sits on one of two executor boundaries; the shared boundary already exists
detail: The `minLength: 1` that admitted `"summary": "test"` lives in `_RAW_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` in harness_labs/controller_live.py:32-48, which BOTH executors emit (controller_live.py:257 and claude_task_executor.py:27,169), and the shared semantic envelope check is `validate_semantic_result` in harness_labs/controller_results.py:37+. CB-07's allowed_paths are `harness_labs/deliverable_floor.py` + `harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py` only, so the Codex/live executor path keeps the hollow-output hole the node exists to close. Tightening the shared schema constraint plus a handful of predicates at the shared validation point is strictly less surface than a new module wired into one caller. Relatedly, AC-CB07-2 pins an implementation file path ('the floor is a closed deterministic rule set in harness_labs/deliverable_floor.py') as an acceptance criterion — that is a design decision hard-coded into the contract, and the closed-rule-set/no-model-judgment property is what actually needs asserting.

title: The red/green gate cannot enforce the one property the program says it must — and fails in exactly the way CB-03 diagnoses
detail: scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:74-83 accepts ANY nonzero pytest exit as 'red'. Collection errors, ImportError, missing fixtures, and environment faults all satisfy it, so the plan's central rule ('Finding tests must fail on base because of behavior, not ImportError' — plan lines 20-23, restated in every implementer prompt at run_burden_plan_graph.py:386-387) is prose with no mechanism behind it, and no acceptance criterion asserts it. The risk is not hypothetical: the base tree is materialized by `git archive` into a temp dir (red_green_check.py:56-72), which is NOT a git repository and gets no install/dependency step, so any base-tree finding test that touches repo/worktree machinery errors out and scores red for free. This is the same 'environmental failure counted as a real failure' confusion CB-03 exists to remove, reproduced in the program's own gate. Minimum fix within the existing apparatus: parse the pytest exit code (5 = no tests collected, 2/3 = usage/internal error) and reject collection errors in the red phase, and assert the specific finding test node ids reported as failed rather than a process-level nonzero. Copying only the node's new finding tests into the base tree is otherwise sound and minimal — that part of the apparatus does not need replacing.
affects: scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:56-83; every node's AC-*-final red/green criterion; docs/development/CONTRACT_BURDEN_RELAXATION_PLAN.md:12-23

title: The RB ledger is inert for this program, so CB-04 duplicates budget accounting instead of riding on it
detail: Program rule 3 claims 'this run is itself a recovery-system live test' with the RB `RetryBudgetLedger`. But the launcher constructs `FeatureRunOutcome(status=..., candidate_commit=..., plan_graph_id=..., plan_node_id=..., feature_run_id=..., run_dir=...)` with no `evidence` field (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:665-672; the field defaults to None at harness_labs/plan_graph.py:375). `import_child_evidence` is therefore skipped entirely (plan_graph.py:1192), and the ledger sees only launch reservations — never gate invocations, repair dispatches, or classifications. Consequences for necessity: (a) the claimed live test of the recovery system is not exercised; (b) CB-04 builds a second, independent repair-accounting system inside feature_run.py, while `_CLASS_LIMITS`/`_assert_capacity` (plan_graph_budget.py:47-54,464-478) already meters repair dispatches per class per node and `_failure_keys` (plan_graph_budget.py:479-491) already provides stable per-finding keys — which is precisely the substrate diagnosis item 7 says to delta-scope ON ('make the repair budget delta-scoped on the RB ledger'). As scoped, CB-04 duplicates rather than extends.

title: AC-CB04-2's 'hard cap' is a third bound over two that already exist
detail: The verification loop is already hard-bounded by `for ordinal in range(1, repair_limit + 4)` (harness_labs/feature_run.py:1329), and the ledger independently caps repair dispatches by class (`node_gate_limit=5` / `infra_limit=3`, plan_graph_budget.py:29-54,464-470). Adding a separately-declared, separately-audited cap gives three bounds with three failure messages and no stated precedence. The existing loop bound generalizes for free: make it a function of the renewal rule rather than introducing a new declared constant.

title: AC-CB01-3 adds an enum member the diagnosis offered as the more expensive of two options
detail: Diagnosis item 4 (contract-burden-reduction.md:44) offers 'add a `plan` source OR map binding criteria to it inside `run_plan_graph_feature_worktree` so callers cannot get it wrong'. The plan takes the first, widening the closed enum at harness_labs/controller_kernel.py:1222-1224, even though this program's own launcher works today with `"source": "operator"` (run_burden_plan_graph.py:568) and nothing consumes the source value differentially. The load-bearing half of the criterion is the second clause — stop tests/test_feature_run.py mocking past the real kernel path — which needs no new vocabulary. As written, one criterion bundles an avoidable enum widening with a test fix.

title: AC-CB01-4 is the largest new mechanism in CB-01 for the smallest evidence, and a widening would do
detail: Diagnosis item 6 is self-labelled 'minor' (contract-burden-reduction.md:60) with a single exp-1 occurrence, yet AC-CB01-4 asks for identity minting on rejected dispatches plus journal recording plus provenance acceptance. The rejection is already an event in the hash chain; the gate that refuses it is one check — `if not self.evidence.contains(ref): return "unknown_evidence"` (harness_labs/controller_kernel.py:426-428). Letting that check also accept refs that resolve to existing audit-journal events is a widening of an existing predicate, not new substrate, and the diagnosis says as much ('they exist in the hash chain regardless').

title: Preservation criteria restate behavior the named regression targets already cover
detail: AC-CB02-2 enumerates five rejections the validator must still perform — unknown section keys, unassigned/unknown-run criteria, unknown or cyclic dependencies, empty allowed_paths, out-of-scope path intents — every one of which is existing code (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:1897-1945, cycle detection at 1867-1887) already guarded by `tests/test_plan_graph.py`, which is CB-02's declared regression target. The same holds for the second half of AC-CB03-3. These criteria can only be 'proved' by tests that pass on base, so they add red/green ceremony without adding evidence. Regression targets are the right instrument for preservation; acceptance criteria should carry only the delta.

title: Fully serial dependency chain adds avoidable blocking surface between nodes that share no files
detail: CB-01..CB-07 are chained linearly (contract-burden-decomposition.json depends_on fields; run_burden_plan_graph.py NODES). Only some edges are real: CB-03/CB-04/CB-05/CB-06 genuinely contend over harness_labs/feature_run.py, and CB-01/CB-06 over controller_kernel.py. CB-02 (harness_labs/plan_graph.py) shares no file with CB-01, and CB-07 shares only claude_task_executor.py with CB-05. Given that a blocked node blocks everything downstream and the diagnosis's dominant observed cost is whole-graph relaunch (contract-burden-reduction.md:64,75), each unnecessary edge is real risk surface. The invented edges should be dropped or justified.
